case_name: Karam Kaur v Jalandhar Improvement Trust and others
facts: The case is about a dispute between Karam Kaur (wife of original plaintiff Ramesh Chander) and Jalandhar Improvement Trust over the allotment of a plot in a scheme known as '55 acres development scheme'.
Ramesh Chander, the original plaintiff, died on 14th December, 2003. His widow, Karam Kaur, filed an appeal to bring her on record as the legal heir.
The High Court rejected the applications for condonation of delay in bringing LRs on record and setting aside the order dismissing the appeal in default.
issues: Whether the delay in bringing the legal representatives (LRs) on record was justified?
Whether the High Court correctly rejected the applications for condonation of delay and setting aside the order dismissing the appeal in default?
petitioner_arguments: The appellant, Karam Kaur, argued that she had no knowledge about the dismissal of the appeal for non-prosecution.

She claimed to be an illiterate lady who was informed by her husband that his appeal was not likely to be taken up for the next 20 years and their counsel would intimate the date whenever it is listed.
respondent_arguments: The respondents, Jalandhar Improvement Trust, argued that the delay in bringing the LRs on record was unjustified.
They claimed that Karam Kaur had knowledge of the pendency of the second appeal and should have filed a petition for substitution earlier.
court_reasoning: The court held that it was not a fit case to condone delay, bring the LRs on record and set aside the order of abatement.
It found that Karam Kaur had knowledge of the pendency of the second appeal and should have filed a petition for substitution earlier.
holding: The High Court's judgment rejecting the applications for condonation of delay and setting aside the order dismissing the appeal in default was upheld.
